newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-WestLB 96 profit up, upbeat for 97.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-WestLB 96 profit up, upbeat for 97.

text.p: Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale (WestLB), the acquisitive German public bank, on Tuesday reported a 10.3 percent rise in 1996 net profit amid gains from its expanding investment banking business.

The bank, Germany's largest publicly-owned regional bank or Landesbank, also said it was optimistic for 1997 after operating profit before risk provisions had risen by 7.5 percent in the first quarter.
"It isn't possible to extrapolate a full-year forecast from the first-quarter results but the start was positive," said chief executive Friedel Neuber.
Group net profit last year rose to 736 million marks ($433.4 million) from 667 million marks. Operating profit after risk provisions was up 10.6 percent at 1.39 billion marks.
Earnings were driven by income gains at London-based unit West Merchant Bank and by the first-time consolidation of British stockbroker Panmure Gordon & Co Ltd, WestLB said.
WestLB's travel subsidiary Thomas Cook also contributed to the rise.
Neuber said WestLB had expanded its trading and issuing of non-mark denominated debt in London, while mark-denominated business remained concentrated at the bank's Duesseldorf headquarters.

Last year's purchase of the asset management business of Quorum Capital Management Ltd had helped strengthen WestLB's position in London and the bank had also increased its presence in the Asia-Pacific region, opening offices in Shanghai and Sydney.
WestLB said it planned to continue expanding its investment banking activities in 1997 and would also invest in risk management systems.
"We are in talks with a number of banks in Europe aimed at cooperating more closely but that does not mean we will take stakes," Neuber said.
Own-account trading income in 1996 jumped by 59.2 percent to 458 million marks with trading in equities and derivative instruments yielding heavy income gains, WestLB.
Net commission income rose 18.6 percent to 1.65 billion marks while net interest income advanced 3.2 percent to 3.93 billion marks.

WestLB conceded that the drive into investment banking had sharply increased spending on staff and risk management systems, with staff costs up 12.8 percent at 2.52 billion marks and other costs up 29 percent to 2.26 billion.
The group's balance sheet total grew by 9.8 percent to 470.8 billion marks while lending was up 10 percent at 413.7 billion marks.

Separately, Neuber, who is also president of the Federal Association of Public Banks, again denied charges by the private banks that the public banks were enjoying an unfair competitive advantage over them.
The private banks allege 11 billion marks of state capital transferred to publicly-owned regional banks since 1990 were in breach of European Union subsidy rules.
Germany's private sector bank association said on Tuesday it expected the EU to start probing the allegations in June.

The dispute dates back to a complaint filed by the private banks with the EU Commission in 1994 and could call Germany's giant public sector banking system into question if the EU decides to investigate.
